q1_issues.issue: "his retirement" is a possessive on an event nominal, which the genitive rule encodes as (Possession …); the temporal-anchor rule also says an anchor event-noun gets its class atom and the ordering relation and nothing else.
(Inheritance …_secretary_… assistant) exposes a modifier that fails the compound-concepts predication test ("*the secretary is assistant"), so the modifier genus should not have been emitted.
(Member ronald_reagan president) asserts a kind from a title the Names-and-casing rule treats as surface only, to be kept inside the Name string (cf. (Name okoro "Dr Okoro") with no doctor atom).

q2_gaps: a multi-word office title carrying PP arguments ("assistant secretary of energy for defense programs"): Compound concepts covers only modifier_noun fusion, so nothing licenses fusing a title with of/for complements into one symbol, nor says how those complements should otherwise attach

the possessive subject of an event nominalization ("his retirement", "her resignation"): only the of-phrase OBJECT of a nominalization and the plain Possession genitive are covered, not the underlying agent
an occupational/office title before a name ("President Ronald Reagan"): the title rule fixes the Name string but does not say whether a companion kind atom is also licensed
notes: As and Under are preposition-named obliques on the event and are licensed; the "after"-clause correctly gets Before with no connective atom and no tense on the anchor. Experiencer for the stative "served" is defensible under the intransitive-subject test.
